full_judgment:
A TM Afzal J: The appellants, father and son respectively, are accused of an offence under section 420 Penal Code in Petition Case No. 176C of 1983 pending in the Court of a Magistrate, First Class, Faridpur. They went for quashing of the proceeding under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure obtained Rule but the High Court Division (Dhaka Bench) by judgment and order dated 23rd June 1986 discharged the Rule. This appeal by leave is from the said judgment and order. 

 3. The Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Faridpur by his order dated 1.2.83 took cognizance of the offence under section 420 Penal Code and issued warrant of arrest against the appellants. As already noticed, the High Court Division refused to quash the proceeding pending against the appellants by the impugned order. Leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division took a proper view of the facts and law involved in the case in rejecting the prayer for quashing of the proceeding. 

 i. The complainant filed a petition of complaint earlier on 23.3.82 making the same allegation (as in the present case) and cognizance was taken under sections 406/420 Penal Code in Petition Case No.663C of 1982, In that case an order of discharge was passed on 18.8,82 under section 250(h) CrPC. 

 ii. During the pendency of the said case the complainant approached the District Martial Law Administrator, Khulna with the same allegation and the accused appellant No.1 was asked to appear before the DMLA. He produced receipt showing payment of Tk.45,000/- to Biswanath Ghose on 23.9.80 who is admittedly a business partner of the complainant. On perusal of the said receipt the Martial Law Authority settled the matter making appellant No.1 to pay a further sum of Tk. 20,000/- in full satisfaction of the complainant's claim. Appellant No.1 paid Tk.20,000/- against the receipt granted by the complainant on 30.6.82. 

 iii. Appellant No.1 is the sole proprietor of M/s Mahbub Brothers and has been carrying on Jute Business at Daulatpur; his son, appellant No.2, is neither a partner of the firm nor connected in any way with the business of the firm. The complainant with ill-motive made his son an accused in the case although he has nothing to do with the business of the firm. 

 6. The complainant-respondent has not appeared to contest this appeal and it appears that he also did not contest the proceeding in revision. The facts alleged by the appellants as referred to above may, therefore, be accepted as uncontested. Be that as it may, we think a consideration of the facts stated in the petition of complaint alone will be sufficient for disposing of the question as to whether any proceeding under section 420 or under any other section of the Penal Code or any other law defining crime is maintainable against the appellants. It will be seen from the petition of complaint that the parties were traders in jute and that the appellants bought jute from the complainant on different dates, sometimes on credit and sometimes on payment of cash and on accounting after the end of the year, the complainant claims, there was an outstanding due from the appellants to the tune of Tk.83,700/-. Admittedly appellant No.1 issued three cheques in favour of the partner of the complainant but as there was no money in the account, the appellant paid Tk.15,000/- in cash upon taking back two of the cheques. These statements clearly show that the parties were in usual business transaction over a period of time which at times was carried on the basis of trust. The claim of money made by the complainant was not the out-come of a particular transaction between strangers or of any representation dishonestly or fraudulently made by the appellant, rather the alleged claim arose after the accounting was made at the end of the year following regular business intercourse between the parties. It is clear that the complainant had no occasion to disbelieve the appellants in supplying jute to them at times on credit and this is nothing uncommon in business transactions. If upon settlement of accounts at the end of a stipulated period, it is found that some money is due to one party from the other and the said other party fails to pay the amount then the liability which ensues is undisputably one of civil nature and by no stretch of imagination it can be said that the liability for non-payment is also criminal. Indeed there is no allegation in the present case that the appellants fraudulently or dishonestly induced the complainant by practicing deception upon them to deliver the goods (jute) to them. The supply was made by the complainant, according to his own statement, sometimes on cash payment and sometimes on credit. In such circumstances it is impossible to hold, even if it is accepted as true that a certain sum of money remained due to the complainant after accounting was made at the end of a certain period, that there was an offence of cheating committed by the appellants. The complainant specifically alleged that “অসদুদ্দেশ্যে প্রনোদিত হইয়া তাহারা টাকা বাকী ফেলিয়া আমাদের টাকা আত্মসাৎ করিয়াছেন আগে জানিলে আমরা কথনই উক্ত আসামীদের বাকীতে কোন মাল দিতাম না। আসামীগণ উক্ত ৬৮,৭০০/- টাকা আত্মসাৎ করিয়া দঃবিঃ ৪০৬ ধারায় অপরাধ করিয়াছেন।” 

 7. It will be seen that the impugned proceeding in the facts and circumstances of the case is entirely misconceived because the allegation that the dues were allowed to accrue dishonestly does neither attract an offence under section 420 nor under section 406 Penal Code or under any other section. We have therefore no hesitation to hold that the High Court Division was not at all justified in finding "that the dispute though arose from a business transaction but for that alone it cannot be said that the same is of a Civil nature". The ingredients of the offence of cheating or of misappropriation have not been properly considered by the High Court Division in the context of the facts alleged in the petition of complaint and thus it allowed itself to fall into an error.
